svg.title: HyperWeave — unframed hero, adaptive
svg.desc: HyperWeave hero banner, adaptive: two caustic field groups gated by prefers-color-scheme over a single lockup whose paints are routed through CSS custom properties, so the wordmark outline is stored exactly once.

hw:reasoning.hw:intent: One file for surfaces that flip, without storing the wordmark outline twice.
hw:reasoning.hw:approach: The field is the only thing duplicated: two background groups, .sch-l and .sch-d, carrying their own substrate, blooms, field opacities and vignette hue. Everything above the field renders exactly once. Every scheme-dependent paint on the lockup is routed through a CSS custom property, so the mark, the wordmark path and the subtitle each exist as a single element whose fill, stroke and filter resolve per scheme. The filter pair is shared: cherenkov uses the same lighting colours in both schemes, so only the rect opacities differ and one caustA/caustB pair drives both groups. The light values also sit on the elements as presentation attributes, which means a renderer that drops CSS entirely still emits a correct light hero rather than an unpainted one.
hw:reasoning.hw:tradeoffs: The custom-property routing has a failure mode worse than no CSS at all: a renderer that parses CSS but does not support var() computes fill as unset rather than falling back to the presentation attribute, which paints the lockup black. resvg and older librsvg are the exposure. Surfaces that never flip should embed the native emission instead — this file exists for the ones that do. The .sch-d group is hidden by a display attribute rather than only by CSS so a CSS-blind renderer does not stack both fields. Weight is roughly 1.6x a native file, all of it field. The shared filter pair means the right-biased light orbits tuned for the light field also drive the dark one, a small divergence from the dark-native emission paid for halving the filter count. Reduced motion remains unresolved.
hw:reasoning.hw:spatial-notes: Lockup metrics identical to both native emissions: mark translate(146,150) scale 1.20; wordmark translate(222.82,-724.6) scale 1.58 with H flush x284; subtitle x284 y227.4. Vignette sides 120, top and bottom 72, drawn per scheme group in that scheme substrate hue.

svg.text: The artifact layer for agent-human representations
